sections.h2: What a carpenter or joiner can help with
sections.html:
• Hanging internal and external doors
  • Fitted wardrobes, alcove units and shelving
  • Wooden flooring and skirting
  • Staircases and balustrades
  • Roof timbers, stud walls and first-fix carpentry on building projects

• You want made-to-measure storage or furniture
  • You are renovating and need doors, skirting and architrave fitted
  • You are building an extension or converting a loft

• Fire doors (for example in loft conversions or flats) must be installed correctly to work; ask about experience with certified fire door sets.
  • Look at a portfolio of finished work, especially bespoke pieces.
  • Agree materials: solid timber, MDF or veneered board.
  • Membership of a body such as the Institute of Carpenters is a good sign.

Prices vary from job to job. The main factors are:

  • Bespoke versus off-the-shelf items
  • Materials and finishes
  • Size and complexity of the job
  • Painting or finishing included
  • Removal of old fittings

Every job is different, so the only reliable way to know the price for your home is to get at least three written, itemised quotes for the same scope of work and compare them like for like.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a carpenter and a joiner?
faqs.a: In the UK, joiners traditionally make timber items such as windows, doors and stairs in a workshop, while carpenters fit and build on site. Many tradespeople do both.

faqs.q: Can a carpenter fit a fire door?
faqs.a: Yes, if they are experienced with fire doors. The door, frame, hinges, seals and gaps all need to be correct for the door to perform in a fire.
Many carpenters fit wooden and laminate flooring. Ask whether the price includes underlay, skirting and removing old flooring.
